messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — AuroraHW reached out about a joint perf/W + throughput benchmark for their new 48GB board. They want a public writeup + a marketplace tile. Can we sync on the test matrix next week?
jon.p: +1. Proposed matrix: Llama-2-70B and LLaMA-3-70B (FP16, INT8, INT4 if stable), seq lenses [512, 2048], batch sizes [1,4,8], and kernel variants (stock, tuned). Measure tokens/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, and Joules/token.
kevin.l: Add GPU temp and thermal throttling checks. Kernel flags we should try: --fused-attn=true, --use-vectorized-kernels=true, and our optimized sparse matmul path. Also record CUDA/driver versions.
sara.t: I can own infra + CI. Need a reproducible run container + a single script that emits csv + JSON summary + perf traces. We'll add a GH Actions job that uploads artifacts to the bench bucket.
alex.aurora: AuroraHW can provide 6 test nodes (48GB cards) and PDUs for per-rack power. We'll run their internal power-collector and share CSVs. Important: we need NTP sync and a sample script to call from our runner.
maria.g: Great. Two publishing goals: 1) joint technical blog that explains tuning wins and methodology, 2) marketplace tile with a performance profile and recommended config. We should avoid any single-claim bragging — focus on reproducibility and fair comparison.
jon.p: For fairness, include both single-card and 4-card runs, and show scaling curves. Also run our baseline (Redwood default runtime) + Aurora tuned kernels.
kevin.l: Quick run command I'd like to validate (example):
```
./run_bench --model llama-3-70b \n  --precision int8 \n  --seq 2048 \n  --batch 4 \n  --cuda-flags "--fused-attn --use-vectorized-kernels" \n  --telemetry out/telemetry.json \n  --power-log /mnt/pdu/power.csv
```
sara.t: Perfect. I'll wrap that in docker:registry/redwood/bench:aurora-sync and a GH Actions workflow. We'll validate that telemetry json schema matches our bench dashboard.
alex.aurora: We'll also provide rack PDU mapping and sample IPMI commands. We'll need timeline: can you share kernel build options if we want to drop in tuned kernels?
maria.g: We should create a shared repo (bench/aurorahw-joint) with clear runbook and a checklist for publish (data CSVs, raw traces, config, AMI/container hash, and contact roster).
marketing.jess: Heads-up from marketing: target audience is infra/platform engineers. We'll draft a short customer-friendly explainer + graphs. Please flag any embargo windows.
jon.p: Action items: assign tickets — 1) infra CI, 2) runbook + script, 3) data ingestion + dashboard, 4) blog draft, 5) marketplace artifact. Can someone pick 2 & 3?
sara.t: I'll pick infra CI (ticket #BENCH-432).
kevin.l: I'll own data ingestion + dashboard (ticket #BENCH-433). I'll add metric names: tokens_per_second, joules_per_token, p99_ms, kernel_version.
maria.g: @alex.aurora can you confirm nodes and PDU access by Monday? Also need contact for on-call during runs.
alex.aurora: Confirmed. I'll give user accounts and a small runbook. On-call is me + engops at Aurora.
benchbot: benchmark-runner: job 8421 started on 1834000200 (sanity check run, model=llama-3-70b, seq=512, batch=1). Artifacts will be uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/aurora-sync/sanity/8421/
maria.g: Let's aim for initial sanity runs Tue, full sweeps Wed/Thu next week. We'll iterate on kernel flags and publish a draft by the following Friday.
marketing.jess: I'll reserve Friday the week after for announcement. If data looks good we can coordinate a joint press blurb.
jon.p: One more technical note — include KV-cache warmup for chat-style traces. For throughput vs perf/W, ensure we test both cold-start and steady-state.
kevin.l: Also add a short regression test in our eval harness to prevent performance regressions in later builds.
maria.g: OK — I'll spin up the repo and create the tickets. Thanks everyone — syncing in #partnerships next Monday at 10am PT to confirm resources.
